domain: Political Economy / Social Policy / Labor Markets
topic_summary: Analysis of Universal Basic Income as a contested kernel where the same income-support commitment is read as either a freedom-floor (enabling autonomy and risk-taking) or a dependency-trap (eroding work incentives and creating state dependence). Each reading instantiates structurally different constraints with distinct beneficiary/victim structures and extractiveness profiles.

key_entities: Universal Basic Income (unconditional cash transfer to all citizens)
Labor market (employment structure and wage dynamics)
Welfare state apparatus (existing means-tested transfer systems)
Precarious workers (gig economy, part-time, informal sector participants)
Capital holders (employers, investors benefiting from wage suppression)
State fiscal capacity (tax base and transfer sustainability)
key_tensions: Autonomy enhancement vs work disincentive (freedom-floor vs dependency-trap readings)
Unconditional transfer vs means-tested targeting (universalism vs efficiency)
key_mechanisms: Income floor effect (minimum guaranteed income altering reservation wages)
Labor supply response (behavioral change in work hours and job acceptance)
Fiscal sustainability constraint (tax revenue requirements vs transfer obligations)
absences: Inflation transmission mechanism (how UBI affects price levels and real purchasing power)
Monopsony power dynamics (employer wage-setting power in thin labor markets)

commitment_system_recognition.kernel_description: Unconditional income support as a policy commitment stabilizing citizen economic security
commitment_system_recognition.authority_description: State fiscal and legislative authority to tax and transfer

readings.commitment: Income support as autonomy-enabling floor that expands choice sets
readings.authority_grounding: Liberal autonomy / capability approach / labor market power rebalancing
readings.expected_structural_delta: Workers enter beneficiary set via expanded exit options; employers enter victim set via reduced monopsony power; moderate extractiveness from tax base

readings.commitment: Income support as work-disincentive creating state dependence
readings.authority_grounding: Work ethic / human capital theory / fiscal conservatism
readings.expected_structural_delta: State enters beneficiary set via expanded client base; workers enter victim set via skill atrophy and reduced earnings; high extractiveness from future productivity

readings.commitment: Income support as employer subsidy enabling wage suppression
readings.authority_grounding: Marxian labor theory / monopsony analysis / fiscal sociology
readings.expected_structural_delta: Capital holders enter beneficiary set via socialized wage floor; workers ambiguous (income floor vs wage suppression); high extractiveness from public fiscal capacity

axes.structural_delta: Unconditional income floor expands worker choice sets and rebalances labor market power
axes.primary_observable: Reservation wage changes; job acceptance rates for low-quality work; entrepreneurship entry rates; care work time allocation
axes.selection_reason: First reading of contested kernel; distinct beneficiary structure (workers gain exit power)

axes.structural_delta: Unconditional income reduces work incentives and creates long-term state dependence
axes.primary_observable: Labor force participation rates; hours worked; skill acquisition rates; intergenerational welfare dependency
axes.selection_reason: Second reading of contested kernel; opposite victim structure (workers harmed via atrophy)

axes.structural_delta: UBI functions as public subsidy to low-wage employers by socializing the wage floor
axes.primary_observable: Wage distribution changes post-UBI; employer labor cost reductions; public expenditure as share of total compensation
axes.selection_reason: Third reading of contested kernel; highest centrality via fiscal extraction dimension

axes.human_readable: Inflation Transmission (Price-Level Response to Income Floor)
axes.structural_delta: Universal income floor triggers price increases that erode real purchasing power
axes.primary_observable: CPI changes post-implementation; rent inflation in housing markets; wage-price spiral indicators
axes.selection_reason: Deferred: affects all readings but is upstream mountain; token budget prioritizes contested readings

axes.human_readable: Fiscal Sustainability Constraint (Tax Base vs Transfer Obligations)
axes.structural_delta: UBI requires tax increases that may exceed politically feasible or economically sustainable levels
axes.primary_observable: Required tax rates for full UBI funding; tax base elasticity; political support thresholds
axes.selection_reason: Deferred: coordination constraint but lower structural distinctiveness than kernel readings

deferred_axes.structural_delta: Price-level response to universal income floor
deferred_axes.deferral_reason: Upstream mountain affecting all readings; deferred to preserve token budget for contested kernel analysis

deferred_axes.structural_delta: Tax base capacity vs transfer obligations
deferred_axes.deferral_reason: Coordination constraint with lower structural distinctiveness than kernel readings

omegas.description: Do the three readings actually emit different constraints, or do they collapse under empirical scrutiny? If labor supply is inelastic and wage suppression dominates, subsidy_capture_reading absorbs the other two.

If inflation_transmission mountain fully erodes real purchasing power, all three readings may reduce to the same null constraint (no real income change). Deferred axis may invalidate kernel structure.
omegas.source: Dark Matter Probe 2 (Absence Inventory) + deferred axis inflation_transmission

omegas.description: At what level of employer market power does freedom_floor flip to subsidy_capture? The threshold is empirically contested and may vary by labor market segment.
omegas.source: Dark Matter Probe 3 (Beneficiary Scan) + absence: monopsony power dynamics

omegas.description: Existing UBI pilots (Kenya, Finland, Stockton) operate at scales where general equilibrium effects (inflation, wage suppression) do not manifest. Extrapolation to national scale is structurally uncertain.

fracture_scan.notes: F34 detected: Model lacks domain expertise to adjudicate empirical claims about labor supply elasticity, monopsony power distribution, and inflation transmission mechanisms at national scale. Generated omega_pilot_generalizability and omega_empirical_collapse to bound uncertainty. Kernel structure is analytically valid but empirical substrate is contested beyond model's competence.
